article.title: How to Ask for Clarification at Work

paragraphs.en: When instructions sound clear but leave important details open, asking a short question can prevent hours of rework. A useful question names the uncertain point and offers a concrete interpretation. Instead of saying 'I do not understand,' you can ask 'Should the report cover only this month, or also the previous month?' Clarification is not a sign of weakness. It shows attention to the result and respect for other people's time.
paragraphs.zh: 本段討論「How to Ask for Clarification at Work」的實務含義：先理解問題與決策背景。 重要的是將觀察到的現象與真正需要採取的行動分開，並留下可供驗證的依據。
paragraphs.ja: 「How to Ask for Clarification at Work」について、業務上の前提と意思決定を確認する。まず課題と背景を理解する。 観察事実と実際に取るべき行動を区別し、検証可能な根拠を残すことが重要である。

paragraphs.en: At the start of a meeting, explain what you already know. Then identify the missing information and propose a choice. This helps colleagues answer quickly. After the meeting, write down the decision, responsible person, and deadline. A short written confirmation can prevent different memories of the same conversation. When the situation changes, ask again rather than relying on an outdated assumption.
paragraphs.zh: 本段討論「How to Ask for Clarification at Work」的實務含義：必須確認條件、風險與後續行動，不能只依賴單一表面指標。 重要的是將觀察到的現象與真正需要採取的行動分開，並留下可供驗證的依據。
